metaDescription: Six large rice cookers for crowds and batch cooking: 20-cup digital multicookers, a 30-cup steamer and a 40-cup commercial warmer compared side by side.
expertTake: The AROMA Professional Plus ARC-5000SB is the best 20-cup pick because it combines a digital panel, a steamer and a slow cook mode in one 5 quart pot. The Dash 20-cup is the value pick for a plain one-touch cooker. Skip a 20-cup machine if you cook for fewer than five people, because the pot is too big to cook small amounts well.
introParagraphs: A 20-cup rice cooker is built for a crowd or a weekly batch. Most of the machines sold at this size are cooked-rice figures, which means about 10 cups of dry rice in a 5 quart pot, and a few reach 30 or 40 cups for events and commercial use.

At this scale the questions change. Counter footprint, lid weight, how long a full pot takes to cool and what happens when you cook only a third of the pot all start to matter. We evaluated each machine on honest capacity labelling, control depth and how awkward it is to wash.

products.name: AROMA Professional Plus ARC-5000SB 20-Cup Digital Cooker
products.description:
The ARC-5000SB is the broadest large cooker in this group. A digital panel drives rice, a built-in steam function and a slow cook mode, and the stainless exterior keeps the bulky body looking presentable on a counter. Its listing states a yield range of 4 to 20 cups cooked, which is the honest way to describe a machine whose bottom limit is as important as its top.

Because it is a programmable cooker and not a fuzzy logic design, the cycles follow set times and temperatures. That is fine for a full or nearly full pot, but a four cup load in a 5 quart pot will cook less evenly than a Zojirushi would. The slow cook function is an advantage for chili or jambalaya, though it is gentler than a dedicated slow cooker. Against the AROMA Professional with 10 modes, this model leans on steaming and the stainless shell.

The lid carries condensation, so lift it away from the body to keep water off the panel. Wash the lid, steam tray and pot by hand soon after serving, since 20 cups of cooked rice leaves a thick starch film. Dry the outside of the pot before sliding it back in and keep the plate free of grains.
products.bestFor: Large families who also want steaming and slow cooking.
pros: Digital controls with steam and slow cook
One pot for jambalaya or rice dinners
cons: Preset cycles struggle with very small loads
Large footprint on a standard counter

products.name: AROMA Professional 20-Cup Digital Cooker, 5 Qt, 10 Modes
products.description:
What distinguishes this AROMA from the ARC-5000SB is its Saute-then-Simmer program, which lets you sear and soften ingredients on high heat and then drop to a simmer in the same pot. Ten modes, smart sensors and a removable steam tray turn it into a one-pot machine for risotto, pilaf or a stew over rice. The 5 quart pot holds up to 20 cups, so it behaves as a large slow cooker with rice skills.

The flip side is that rice quality is not the sole objective. The saute function is not as powerful as a stovetop, and browning is modest in a nonstick pot. If your only goal is plain white rice, the Dash or the 20-cup one-touch AROMA does it for less. Many buyers will find the extra modes more useful than the rice program itself.

To keep the saute mode working, deglaze the pot after browning and wash it before the fond sets. Use only plastic or wooden tools. Wipe the steam tray, check the lid seal, and avoid leaving a heavy pot full of rice on keep warm overnight, because large volumes stay hot and dry slowly.
products.bestFor: Cooks who want to saute, simmer and cook rice in one pot.
pros: 5 quart pot doubles as a slow cooker
cons: Browning is modest in a nonstick pot
More modes than a rice-only cook needs

products.name: AROMA ARC-860NGP 20-Cup 5 Qt Nonstick Rice and Grain Cooker
products.description:
The ARC-860NGP is the large AROMA that puts its effort into the pot. A reinforced five-layer Bonded Granite pot is meant to withstand wear better than a thin nonstick coating, and the steamer basket stacks inside the pot for one-dish meals. It states a cooking range of 4 to 20 cups of cooked rice, which is the same honest range as the ARC-5000SB.

Granite style coatings are tough, but no coating is metal-spoon proof. This model also omits the digital panel and slow cook features of its siblings, so you are paying for the pot and a simple cooking cycle. In this lineup, that makes it a plain workhorse for batch cooks who do not want to read a manual.

Treat the pot like a cast pan with a coating: let it cool before washing, avoid scouring pads, and dry it completely. The steamer basket should be rinsed under hot water. Do not stack heavy items on the lid, since a bent lid seats poorly and leaks steam.
products.bestFor: Batch cooks who value a hard-wearing pot over extra modes.

products.name: Dash Family Sized 20-Cup Rice Cooker, Ceramic Nonstick Pot
products.description:
Dash keeps its family-size cooker plain: plug in, add rice and water, start, and the unit holds the rice warm. The removable pot carries a ceramic nonstick coating, and the 10 raw cup, 20 cooked cup capacity is stated right in the title. It is the cheapest way to reach a 20-cup pot in this group.

The trade is the absence of a steam tray in the listing and any program beyond the basic cycle. It also has a lighter build than the stainless AROMA models, so expect more plastic and a shorter service life under daily use. Beside the ARC-860NGP, the Dash gives up the thick pot for a lower entry cost.

Because the shell is lighter, take care not to knock it while hot, and keep the cord out of the path of foot traffic. Rinse rice before cooking to limit foam in the big pot, wipe the lid, and wash the ceramic pot by hand.
products.bestFor: Budget shoppers who need a big pot and nothing more.
pros: Lowest entry cost at this size

products.name: Hamilton Beach 30-Cup Cooked Rice Cooker and Steamer
products.description:
Hamilton Beach pushes the size past 20 cups with a 30 cup cooked, 15 cup raw cooker that includes the brand's steam and rinsing basket. It is the pick for a church supper, a large family gathering or someone who cooks a week of rice at once. The basket is helpful here, because rinsing 15 cups of rice by hand in a bowl is an awkward job.

Cooking by thermal switch means the machine ends the cycle when water has boiled off, and with this much rice the center of the pot can lag the edges. Stir gently after the cycle and let it rest with the lid on. It is also bulky, and the weight of a full pot is something to plan for before lifting.

Rinse the pot immediately because 30 cups of rice leaves a heavy film. Check the vent for grains, and store the basket inside. Use the handles when moving, and never lift a full pot with wet hands.
products.bestFor: Events and big households that need more than 20 cups.
cons: Center of the pot can lag the edges

products.name: AROMA Commercial 20-Cup Raw, 40-Cup Cooked Rice Cooker
products.description:
AROMA's commercial cooker takes 20 cups of raw rice and returns about 40 cups cooked, with a stainless lid, a heavy-duty pot and automatic sensors that track the cook. The one-touch switch is all the control there is. It is the machine for a restaurant counter, a catering table or a very large household.

It is also the least suitable for ordinary kitchens. The pot is so big that cooking under a third of a load will scorch, and the machine needs a dedicated shelf. Compared with the Hamilton Beach 30 cup, it offers a sturdier build and warmer role in exchange for a simpler panel and less convenience.

Plan the cleaning: a pot this size does not fit in most sinks, so you will need a large basin or a hose. Keep the lid seal clear of grains, and let the pot cool before moving. Use a long paddle and never tilt a full pot to pour. Scoop rice out with the paddle instead, and give the stainless lid a wipe because condensation pools in the rim.
products.bestFor: Caterers, community kitchens and very large families.
pros: Acts as a cooker and a warmer
cons: Needs a large sink or basin to wash

buyingCriteria.explanation: A 20-cup cooker usually means 20 cups of cooked rice, which is only 10 cups of raw grain in a 5 quart pot, as the Dash, AROMA ARC-5000SB and ARC-860NGP all show. The Hamilton Beach 30 cup is 15 raw, and the AROMA Commercial is 20 raw and 40 cooked. Check which side of the ratio the number refers to before you choose a size.

A huge pot cooking a small batch scorches the bottom because the rice sits in a thin layer on a big plate. The AROMA ARC-860NGP lists a range of 4 to 20 cups cooked, which tells you the real minimum. Below that range, use a smaller cooker.

The AROMA Professional lines offer modes, timers and saute functions, while the Dash and Hamilton Beach offer a single cycle. A one-touch machine works well when the pot is full. If you also want chili or risotto, the digital models justify the price.

A 5 quart pot filled with 20 cups of cooked rice is heavy, and the 40-cup commercial AROMA is heavier still. Measure the counter, the cabinet height with the lid closed and the route to the sink. A cooker you cannot lift is a cooker you will not use. Look for molded side handles on the housing, since a cooker with no grip points gets pushed across the counter instead of carried.

The ARC-860NGP uses a five-layer granite pot, the Dash uses ceramic nonstick and the commercial AROMA uses a stainless lid over a nonstick pot. Every coating is vulnerable to metal spoons. Choose a pot with a plastic paddle in the box.

A large mass of rice holds heat for hours but also dries at the edges. The commercial AROMA doubles as a warmer, and the others use a basic keep warm plate. For long events, stir the rice and add a splash of water.

howWeEvaluated.description: We separated raw from cooked capacity across six listings, noting that the Hamilton Beach 30 cup is 15 raw and the AROMA Commercial is 20 raw. Clear statements scored higher.

howWeEvaluated.title: Minimum load
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at how small a batch each machine can handle, using the 4 to 20 cup range stated by AROMA as a benchmark.

cards.label: Digital multicooker
cards.text: The AROMA ARC-5000SB and Professional 20-Cup run programs, steam and slow cook. They replace a rice cooker and a small slow cooker, but cost more and take longer to learn.

cards.label: Plain cooker
cards.text: The Dash, Hamilton Beach 30-Cup and ARC-860NGP use a single cycle. They are easier to operate and cheaper, but they only cook rice and steam.

howToChoose.note: Pick a multicooker if you want one pot to do several jobs. Pick plain if rice is the only job.

rows: Lighter pot is easier to wash

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A pot that takes at least 10 raw cups, a lid that comes off without dripping on the panel, and a keep warm that holds rice for a few hours. Plan to portion and refrigerate rice within a few hours of cooking.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The AROMA ARC-860NGP is the plain batch cooker with the toughest pot, and the Hamilton Beach 30-Cup carries the biggest loads.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You want one pot for rice, stews and steaming. The AROMA ARC-5000SB and Professional 20-Cup cover that ground.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You cook plain rice for a big family. The Dash and ARC-860NGP do that without extra modes.

maintenance.why: Large volumes leave a thick starch film that hardens as it cools. Early washing saves scrubbing.
Steam carries starch to the vent. A clogged vent causes sputtering.
Spilled grains burn on the plate. A clean plate heats evenly.
Scratches mean the coating is wearing. Replace the pot when flakes appear.
A big pot is heavy. Loose handles or damaged cords are a hazard.

faq.q: How many people does a 20-cup cooker feed?
faq.a: Twenty cups of cooked rice feeds eight to ten people as a side, or a family of four for several days when the leftovers are portioned and chilled. A 40-cup commercial model feeds twenty or more.
Usually cooked, which means about 10 raw cups. The AROMA Commercial and Hamilton Beach 30 list raw numbers too, so check the title.

faq.q: Can I cook a small amount in a big cooker?
faq.a: Only down to the stated minimum, such as 4 cups cooked on the AROMA 5 quart units. Below that the rice scorches.
The AROMA Professional models do. The Dash and Hamilton Beach cook rice and steam only.

faq.q: How do I wash a 5 quart pot?
faq.a: Soak it while warm, use a soft sponge and avoid scouring pads. A basin helps if the sink is small.

faq.q: How long can a big batch stay on warm?
faq.a: A few hours is fine for most units. Move leftovers to the refrigerator within a few hours of serving, spread in shallow containers so the center of a big batch cools quickly instead of staying warm for hours.
